Refract

/rih-FRAKT/ - rhymes with attract · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Refract means to bend light or waves as they pass from one medium to another.

The telescope's cheap lens refracts blue more sharply than red, leaving a violet fringe around every star.

Worked Example

Highway mirages are honest physics. Air baking above the asphalt grows thin, and light sliding down from the sky refracts as it crosses into that hot layer — each ray bends until what reaches the driver's eye seems to rise off the road ahead, shimmering like standing water that forever keeps its distance.

Refract is the exact word for what the hot air does, because it means to bend light or waves as they pass from one medium to another — the bending happens at the crossing. Deflect would only say the light was knocked off course somehow; refract names the mechanism and the boundary.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

bend: the plain word for the same change of path, boundary or no boundary

redirect: send along a new path by any means at all

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

reflect: bounce it back the way it came instead of bending it through

block: stop the light altogether

Where it sits · how far the light leaves its course — deflect → refract → scatter

deflect vs. refract: Deflect is a single nudge — one ray, one ball, one question knocked slightly off its course by anything in the way.

scatter vs. refract: Scatter goes further than refract — refracted rays bend together, by one rule, while scattered rays fly apart in every direction and the image is lost entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back

Root — fract-

Root — fract-: to break (Latin frangere, fractus)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (back) + fract- (to break) = to break back. A light ray crossing into water is 'broken' at the boundary — its straight path snapped into a new angle. Here re- means back, not again: the beam is bent back off its course, one clean break at the surface.

Use the root in a new word: fraction

Use the root in a new word: fraction: A fraction is a piece broken off a whole number — fract-, 'to break,' doing its plainest work.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / scientific

Refract is the physics word for bending at a boundary — light into water, sound into cold air. Bend covers everything loosely; refract names the mechanism, so keep it for waves crossing from one medium into another. Its neighbor trap is reflect, bounced back and never passed through — an item on this card tests exactly that line. Its unit-mate repulse also sends things back, but repulse turns back an attacker, not a beam.
